diagram_math_checks.check: Eight boundary vertices alternate endpoints/midpoints of the two disjoint vertical attachments with midpoints of the two intervening sectors. Eight center spokes give 4d=8 triangles for d=2, matching step 1.1. Blue attachments each contain two edges. A loop is explicitly described as using two distinct attachments at one vertex, not as identifying intervals.

The two ends each have three boundary vertices, with a midpoint on each long shore, giving eight distinct rim vertices and eight fan triangles as in step 2.1. End intervals have two subdivisions and match the vertex-disk intervals. As step 3.2 permits, the center and both shore midpoints receive the left endpoint label; every rim/spoke endpoint pair then has labels equal or adjacent, so edge distance is at most one.

The cyclic rim q0,q1,...,q7,q0 consists of blue shores q0-q1-q2 and q4-q5-q6 alternating with red vertex sectors q2-q3-q4 and q6-q7-q0. Each occurrence contributes two shore plus two sector edges, so 4k=8 for k=2. The eight fan triangles follow step 2.1. Caption distinguishes the embedded cap rim from its possibly noninjective graph-image characteristic walk, and specifies transport from an abstract disk instead of geometric-center visibility.

A shore with midpoint label u reads u,u,v forwards and v,u,u backwards. Constant vertex sectors insert repetitions only, reproducing step 4.1. No directions or crossings are asserted by the unoriented fan edges; cyclic cap order is explicitly stated. All original numbered proof steps are byte-identical, so the proof remains independent.
